subject: Performance transparency: what we can claim (FP8/INT8 benchmarks)
body:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>, Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2026 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Performance transparency: what we can claim (FP8/INT8 benchmarks)

Irene — we’re updating the “Performance & cost” section in Console and the Optimize recommendations copy (PM-1184 + PM-1185 follow-on). Before we ship UI copy or share excerpts with Sales, can we align on exactly what benchmark claims are approved?

Specifically:
- Can we claim “X% faster” for FP8 vs baseline? If yes, do we need “up to” language and in what cases?
- Which metrics are ok to use publicly: tokens/s, p95 TTFT, p95 TPOT, end-to-end latency?
- Minimum footnotes we need (hardware, model versions, prompt distribution, etc.)

If you already have a template/standard, please send.

Thanks,
Aditya

—

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>, Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2026 at 9:38 AM PT
Subject: Re: Performance transparency: what we can claim (FP8/INT8 benchmarks)

Yes — we should be strict here, especially with the sprint results moving fast and the canary still catching edge cases.

High-level guardrails (aligned w/ our perf standards draft + SRE canary learnings):
1) Avoid absolute universal claims like “FP8 is 30% faster” without tying to a model + GPU + workload regime.
2) Use “up to” only when we also provide the median or a range (e.g., “+8–18% tokens/s”) and we can point to the matrix.
3) Public/external: prefer throughput (tokens/s) and cost proxy deltas per token *for a specified workload*, plus TTFT/TPOT where it’s stable. Avoid “end-to-end latency” unless we define request shape (prompt len, gen len, concurrency).
4) Must include footnotes: model version/hash, runtime version, GPU SKU, driver/CUDA, batching/concurrency, prompt/gen length distribution, warmup rules, and run counts.

I’ll send a concrete approved language block + footnote template by EOD. Elliot — if you want this to read “market-ready” we should do a quick pass together.

Irene

—

From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2026 at 10:07 AM PT
Subject: Re: Performance transparency: what we can claim (FP8/INT8 benchmarks)

+1. A couple things I’d like us to be explicit about so we don’t end up in “gotcha” territory:

- “Top hosted models” ≠ “all models.” We should name the set or at least say “selected hosted models.”
- “H100 numbers” are what most prospects ask for; A100/L4 are where we’ll get questions about whether FP8/INT8 is available + meaningful.
- We should add a standard line about quality: “Quantization settings may affect output quality; Redwood recommends enabling with eval sign-off for sensitive workloads.”

Aditya: for UI copy, we can be a little tighter, but I’d still keep the same footnote standard accessible via “Learn more.”

Elliot

Subject: Re: Performance transparency: what we can claim (FP8/INT8 benchmarks)

Adding one nuance from the Product side:

When we say “tokens/s improved,” we should define whether that’s decode-only, prefill-only, or mixed. Most people read it as “overall.”

Also, we need to be careful claiming TTFT improvements for FP8 attention specifically — there were cases where TTFT regressed depending on scheduler settings and smaller batch sizes.

If helpful I can propose exact phrasing that keeps us honest but still understandable.

Henry

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>, Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2026 at 12:02 PM PT
Subject: Re: Performance transparency: what we can claim (FP8/INT8 benchmarks)

Draft “approved claims” language (internal + external-safe when footnoted):

A) Recommended headline (external-safe):
“On H100 and A100, Redwood’s FP8 and INT8 kernel paths improve throughput on selected hosted models and workloads, while maintaining production rollout safety via canary gating and fallbacks.”

B) Optional quantitative statement (external-safe if constrained):
“For the FP8/INT8 benchmark suite v3 (mixed prefill/decode with production-like prompt and generation length distributions), we observed throughput gains typically in the +8–18% range on H100 for selected models, with workload-dependent variance. Results vary by model architecture, sequence length regime, batch size, and concurrency.”

C) What we should NOT say (until we have broader coverage + more stable canary history):
- “FP8 is faster than baseline across all workloads.”
- “End-to-end latency is improved by X%” without specifying request shape and concurrency.
- “No quality impact” (we can say “quality evaluated; see notes”).

D) Metrics allowed:
- Throughput: tokens/sec (must specify decode-only vs mixed)
- TTFT and TPOT: allowed if we include p50/p95 + sample size, and note scheduler settings
- Error rate / fallback rate: internal only for now

E) Footnote template (minimum) — this is what I want us to standardize on for anything leaving Eng Slack:
1) Model name + version (registry hash) + quantization mode (FP8/INT8) + baseline mode
2) Runtime version + git SHA
3) GPU SKU + driver/CUDA + clocking (locked vs default)
4) Workload definition: prompt length distribution, generation length cap, concurrency, batching window
5) Measurement: warmups, run count, variance reporting (p50/p95 + stddev or CI)
6) Notes: known limitations / excluded regimes (e.g., “FP8 disabled for shape X due to canary regression”)

Attaching the footnote template and metrics defs.

Attachment: benchmark-footnote-template-v2.docx (Google Doc export)
Attachment: fp8-int8-perf-metrics-definitions.pdf

If this looks good, I’ll add a short “How to use these numbers” section for the Optimize UI (tooltip/link).

Irene

Irene — thanks for the template. Let’s ensure Sales uses the same footnote pack when they ask for “H100 numbers.”

Elliot
